## Surveys and roadmaps

Start here to see the whole field at once and to find the papers behind each taxonomy.

- Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey. Peng et al., 2024 arXiv 2408.08921Organizes GraphRAG into graph-based indexing, graph-guided retrieval and graph-enhanced generation, and reviews training, applications and evaluation.Chapters: 3, 33

- Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Graphs (GraphRAG). Han et al., 2024 arXiv 2501.00309A broad survey that defines GraphRAG by five components (query processor, retriever, organizer, generator, data source) and reviews designs domain by domain.Chapters: 14, 33

- A Survey of Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Customized Large Language Models. Zhang et al., 2025 arXiv 2501.13958The survey behind the DEEP-PolyU Awesome-GraphRAG list: knowledge organization, knowledge retrieval and knowledge integration.Chapter: 33

- Unifying Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs: A Roadmap. Pan et al., 2023 arXiv 2306.08302A roadmap for combining LLMs and knowledge graphs: KG-enhanced LLMs, LLM-augmented KGs, and systems where both reason together.Chapters: 5, 20, 33

- Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey. Gao et al., 2023 arXiv 2312.10997The standard survey of plain RAG: naive, advanced and modular RAG, and how retrieval, augmentation and generation are evaluated.Chapters: 1, 2, 22

- Large Language Models on Graphs: A Comprehensive Survey. Jin et al., 2023 arXiv 2312.02783Surveys how LLMs are used on pure, text-attributed and text-paired graphs, as predictors, encoders and aligners.Related chapters: 24, 33

- Demystifying Chains, Trees, and Graphs of Thoughts. Besta et al., 2024 arXiv 2401.14295A taxonomy of reasoning topologies (chains, trees and graphs of thoughts) and how prompting schemes build them. Earlier titled "Topologies of Reasoning".Related chapter: 23

## Foundations: RAG, graph algorithms and graph-LLM interfaces

The classic papers underneath every chapter: retrieval, ranking, community detection, PageRank and how graphs are fed to language models.

- Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. Lewis et al., 2020 arXiv 2005.11401The paper that named retrieval-augmented generation: a retriever and a seq2seq generator trained together for knowledge-intensive tasks.Chapters: 1, 2

- Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering. Karpukhin et al., 2020 arXiv 2004.04906Dense Passage Retrieval: dual encoders trained on question-passage pairs beat BM25 for open-domain QA retrieval.Chapters: 1, 2

- Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks. Reimers and Gurevych, 2019 arXiv 1908.10084Sentence-BERT: siamese BERT networks that produce sentence embeddings comparable with cosine similarity.Chapters: 2, 18

- Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning. Izacard et al., 2021 arXiv 2112.09118Contriever: dense retrievers trained without labels through contrastive learning.Chapter: 17

- ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT. Khattab and Zaharia, 2020 arXiv 2004.12832ColBERT: late interaction keeps one vector per token and scores with MaxSim, between bi-encoders and cross-encoders in cost and quality.Chapters: 31, 33

- Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts. Liu et al., 2023 arXiv 2307.03172Shows models use information at the beginning and end of long contexts better than in the middle, which shapes how context is ordered.Chapters: 1, 7, 18, 22

- Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models. Wei et al., 2022 arXiv 2201.11903Chain-of-thought prompting: showing worked reasoning steps in the prompt improves multi-step reasoning.Related chapter: 23

- ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. Yao et al., 2022 arXiv 2210.03629ReAct: interleaving reasoning traces with tool actions, the loop most graph agents use.Chapters: 3, 23

- The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond. Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009 Foundations and Trends in IRThe definitive explanation of BM25 and BM25F and the probabilistic model behind them.Chapter: 21

- Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods. Cormack et al., 2009 SIGIRIntroduces reciprocal rank fusion, the simple rank-based way to merge result lists used in hybrid retrieval.Chapter: 21

- The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web. Page et al., 1999 Stanford InfoLab technical reportThe original PageRank random-surfer model, the basis of Personalized PageRank retrieval.Chapters: 4, 17

- Finding and evaluating community structure in networks. Newman and Girvan, 2003 arXiv cond-mat/0308217Defines modularity as a measure of community structure and uses it to evaluate divisive clustering.Chapters: 4, 11

- Fast unfolding of communities in large networks. Blondel et al., 2008 arXiv 0803.0476The Louvain method: fast greedy modularity optimization by local moves and aggregation.Chapters: 4, 11

- From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities. Traag et al., 2018 arXiv 1810.08473The Leiden algorithm: adds a refinement phase so communities are guaranteed to be well connected, and runs faster than Louvain.Chapters: 11, 12, 27

- Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs. Malkov and Yashunin, 2016 arXiv 1603.09320HNSW, the layered proximity-graph index behind most approximate nearest neighbor search in vector stores.Chapters: 2, 13

- Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry. Gilmer et al., 2017 arXiv 1704.01212Frames many graph neural networks as message passing neural networks, the vocabulary used for GNN retrievers.Related chapter: 19

- Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks. Kipf and Welling, 2016 arXiv 1609.02907Graph convolutional networks: the simple layer-wise propagation rule most GNN tutorials start from.Chapter: 19

- Attention Is All You Need. Vaswani et al., 2017 arXiv 1706.03762The Transformer architecture. Self-attention cost grows quadratically with input length, one reason context windows are finite and retrieval is needed.Related chapter: 1

- Talk like a Graph: Encoding Graphs for Large Language Models. Fatemi et al., 2023 arXiv 2310.04560Studies how the way a graph is written as text (encoding function, question phrasing, graph structure) changes LLM performance on graph tasks.Chapter: 22

- Let Your Graph Do the Talking: Encoding Structured Data for LLMs. Perozzi et al., 2024 arXiv 2402.05862GraphToken: a trained encoder turns a graph into soft tokens for a frozen LLM, beating hand-written text encodings.Related chapters: 22, 24

- Path-based Algebraic Foundations of Graph Query Languages. Angles et al., 2024 arXiv 2407.04823A formal algebra of paths as the basis of graph query languages such as Cypher and GQL.Related chapters: 5, 20

- Ologs: a categorical framework for knowledge representation. Spivak and Kent, 2011 arXiv 1102.1889Ologs: a category-theory framework for writing knowledge representations precisely, a useful contrast to informal schemas.Related chapter: 5

## Knowledge organization: graph construction, indexing graphs and hierarchies

How text becomes a graph worth searching: extraction, ontologies, tree and community indexes, and cheaper construction.

- From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization. Edge et al., 2024 arXiv 2404.16130Microsoft's GraphRAG: extract an entity graph, detect Leiden communities, write community reports, and answer global questions by map-reduce. The course's central paper.Chapters: 6, 8, 11, 12, 15

- RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval. Sarthi et al., 2024 arXiv 2401.18059RAPTOR: recursively cluster and summarize chunks into a tree, then retrieve across all levels of abstraction.Chapters: 6, 7, 11, 12, 33

- GraphER: A Structure-aware Text-to-Graph Model for Entity and Relation Extraction. Zaratiana et al., 2024 arXiv 2404.12491A text-to-graph model that extracts entities and relations jointly with a structure-aware encoder, an alternative to prompting an LLM.Chapter: 8

- Graphusion: A RAG Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction with a Global Perspective. Yang et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.17600Builds knowledge graphs with a global view: extract candidate triples per document, then fuse and resolve them across the corpus.Chapter: 8

- Docs2KG: Unified Knowledge Graph Construction from Heterogeneous Documents Assisted by Large Language Models. Sun et al., 2024 arXiv 2406.02962Builds a unified knowledge graph from heterogeneous documents (PDFs, web pages, spreadsheets) with layout-aware and LLM-assisted steps.Chapters: 8, 31

- AutoKG: Constructing Virtual Knowledge Graphs from Unstructured Documents for Question Answering. Yu et al., 2020 arXiv 2008.08995An early pipeline that turns unstructured documents into a virtual knowledge graph for question answering.Related chapter: 8

- Increasing the LLM Accuracy for Question Answering: Ontologies to the Rescue!. Allemang and Sequeda, 2024 arXiv 2405.11706Follow-up to the enterprise SQL benchmark: the ontology behind the knowledge graph is used to check generated SPARQL queries and drive an LLM repair step, raising accuracy further.Chapter: 5

- OG-RAG: Ontology-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation For Large Language Models. Sharma et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.15235Grounds retrieval in a domain ontology: facts are organized as ontology-mapped hyperedges and retrieved as compact fact sets.Related chapters: 5, 6

- KAG: Boosting LLMs in Professional Domains via Knowledge Augmented Generation. Liang et al., 2024 arXiv 2409.13731Ant Group's KAG: mutual indexing between a knowledge graph and text chunks, logical-form-guided reasoning, and schema-constrained construction for professional domains.Chapter: 6

- PIKE-RAG: sPecIalized KnowledgE and Rationale Augmented Generation. Wang et al., 2025 arXiv 2501.11551Microsoft's PIKE-RAG: extracts specialized knowledge and builds rationales step by step for industrial domain questions.Related chapters: 6, 32

- Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hierarchical Knowledge. Huang et al., 2025 arXiv 2503.10150HiRAG: builds hierarchical knowledge by clustering entities into summary entities layer by layer, and retrieves across local, bridge and global levels.Chapters: 6, 12

- ArchRAG: Attributed Community-based Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Wang et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.09891ArchRAG: detects attributed communities that use both links and attributes, summarizes them hierarchically, and retrieves with an LLM-guided hierarchical search.Related chapters: 11, 12

- LeanRAG: Knowledge-Graph-Based Generation with Semantic Aggregation and Hierarchical Retrieval. Zhang et al., 2025 arXiv 2508.10391LeanRAG: aggregates entities into semantic clusters with explicit relations between summaries, then retrieves bottom-up along the hierarchy to cut redundancy.Related chapter: 12

- Graph of Records: Boosting Retrieval Augmented Generation for Long-context Summarization with Graphs. Zhang et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.11001Graph of Records: links LLM-generated historical responses to retrieved chunks in a graph and uses a GNN to improve long-context summarization.Related chapter: 12

- SiReRAG: Indexing Similar and Related Information for Multihop Reasoning. Zhang et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.06206SiReRAG: indexes both similar information (semantic trees) and related information (entity-grouped propositions) for multi-hop reasoning.Related chapter: 6

- StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization. Li et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.08815StructRAG: picks the best structure type (table, graph, catalogue, algorithm, chunk) for each task and restructures documents at inference time.Chapter: 6

- You Don't Need Pre-built Graphs for RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Adaptive Reasoning Structures. Chen et al., 2025 arXiv 2508.06105LogicRAG: skips the pre-built graph and instead builds a query-specific logic structure (a DAG of sub-problems) at inference time.Chapter: 33

- AutoGraph-R1: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Knowledge Graph Construction. Tsang et al., 2025 arXiv 2510.15339Trains the graph constructor with reinforcement learning, rewarding graphs by how well they serve downstream RAG.Chapters: 24, 33

- Youtu-GraphRAG: Vertically Unified Agents for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Complex Reasoning. Dong et al., 2025 arXiv 2508.19855Tencent's Youtu-GraphRAG: schema-bounded extraction agents, community detection that fuses structure and semantics, and agentic retrieval in one design.Chapters: 30, 33

- AGRAG: Advanced Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLMs. Wang et al., 2025 arXiv 2511.05549AGRAG: replaces LLM entity extraction with a statistics-based method to avoid hallucinated graphs, and retrieves reasoning paths the LLM can inspect.Related chapter: 8

- KARMA: Leveraging Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Knowledge Graph Enrichment. Lu et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.06472KARMA: nine cooperating LLM agents discover entities, extract relations, align schema and resolve conflicts to enrich an existing knowledge graph.Chapter: 30

## Retrieval: local and global search, PPR, paths, subgraphs, KBQA and hybrid

How to find the right nodes, paths, subgraphs and summaries for a question.

- Introducing DRIFT Search: Combining global and local search methods to improve quality and efficiency. Microsoft Research, 2024 blogDRIFT starts from community reports to draft an answer and follow-up questions, then refines with local search.Chapter: 15

- GraphRAG: Improving global search via dynamic community selection. Microsoft Research, 2024 blogRates community reports top-down with a cheaper model and prunes irrelevant branches before map-reduce.Chapters: 6, 12, 15, 33, C1

- LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Guo et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.05779LightRAG: dual-level retrieval where low-level keywords match entities and high-level keywords match relationships, with incremental graph updates.Chapter: 16

- MiniRAG: Towards Extremely Simple Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Fan et al., 2025 arXiv 2501.06713MiniRAG: a heterogeneous graph of chunks and entities with lightweight topology-driven retrieval, designed so small language models can run RAG.Related chapters: 16, 26

- HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models. Jiménez Gutiérrez et al., 2024 arXiv 2405.14831HippoRAG: OpenIE triples plus synonymy edges form a graph; Personalized PageRank from query entities ranks passages in a single retrieval step.Chapter: 17

- From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models. Jiménez Gutiérrez et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.14802HippoRAG 2: adds passage nodes and deeper query-to-triple linking to HippoRAG, aiming at memory that works for factual, multi-hop and sense-making questions.Chapters: 6, 17, 33, C3

- Don't Forget to Connect! Improving RAG with Graph-based Reranking. Dong et al., 2024 arXiv 2405.18414G-RAG: a GNN reranker over a document graph built from AMR connections, so documents that link to relevant ones are not missed.Chapter: 21

- PathRAG: Pruning Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation with Relational Paths. Chen et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.14902PathRAG: retrieves relational paths between key nodes, prunes them with flow-based pruning, and orders paths by reliability in the prompt.Chapters: 18, 19, 20, 22, 33

- Think-on-Graph: Deep and Responsible Reasoning of Large Language Model on Knowledge Graph. Sun et al., 2023 arXiv 2307.07697Think-on-Graph: the LLM performs beam search over a knowledge graph, exploring and pruning relations and entities until it can answer.Chapter: 18

- Think-on-Graph 2.0: Deep and Faithful Large Language Model Reasoning with Knowledge-guided Retrieval Augmented Generation. Ma et al., 2024 arXiv 2407.10805Think-on-Graph 2.0: alternates knowledge graph exploration with retrieval from linked documents so each guides the other.Chapters: 18, 33

- Plan-on-Graph: Self-Correcting Adaptive Planning of Large Language Model on Knowledge Graphs. Chen et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.23875Plan-on-Graph: decomposes questions into sub-objectives and uses memory and reflection to correct wrong exploration paths on the graph.Chapters: 18, 30, 33

- KG-Agent: An Efficient Autonomous Agent Framework for Complex Reasoning over Knowledge Graph. Jiang et al., 2024 arXiv 2402.11163KG-Agent: a small fine-tuned LLM with a toolbox and memory that reasons over knowledge graphs in an autonomous loop.Related chapters: 18, 30

- Call Me When Necessary: LLMs can Efficiently and Faithfully Reason over Structured Environments. Cheng et al., 2024 arXiv 2403.08593Readi: the LLM writes a full reasoning path up front and only calls the structured environment to edit it when execution fails.Related chapter: 18

- FiDeLiS: Faithful Reasoning in Large Language Model for Knowledge Graph Question Answering. Sui et al., 2024 arXiv 2405.13873FiDeLiS: step-wise beam search over knowledge graph paths with deductive verification of each step.Related chapters: 18, 23

- PolyG: Adaptive Graph Traversal for Diverse GraphRAG Questions. Liu et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.02112PolyG: a taxonomy of four graph question types, the PolyBench benchmark, and adaptive traversal that picks a strategy per question.Chapter: 30

- G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering. He et al., 2024 arXiv 2402.07630G-Retriever: prize-collecting Steiner tree subgraph retrieval plus a GNN soft prompt for question answering over textual graphs.Chapters: 19, 21, 24, 33

- GRAG: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Hu et al., 2024 arXiv 2405.16506GRAG: retrieves textual subgraphs rather than isolated entities and passes them to the LLM as both text and graph embeddings.Chapter: 19

- GNN-RAG: Graph Neural Retrieval for Large Language Model Reasoning. Mavromatis and Karypis, 2024 arXiv 2405.20139GNN-RAG: a GNN finds candidate answers in a KG subgraph; shortest paths to them are verbalized for the LLM.Chapters: 19, 20, 24, 33

- GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation. Luo et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.01113GFM-RAG: a graph foundation model (query-dependent GNN) trained on many graphs, retrieving multi-hop evidence in one step on unseen datasets.Chapters: 19, 24, 33

- Graph Neural Network Enhanced Retrieval for Question Answering of LLMs. Li et al., 2024 arXiv 2406.06572GNN-Ret: builds a passage graph from structural and keyword links and uses a GNN to retrieve related passages together.Related chapter: 19

- SimGRAG: Leveraging Similar Subgraphs for Knowledge Graphs Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Cai et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.15272SimGRAG: the LLM turns the question into a graph pattern, then retrieves the most similar subgraphs by a graph semantic distance.Related chapter: 19

- Simple Is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Li et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.20724SubgraphRAG: a lightweight MLP with structural distance features scores triples, and the retrieved subgraph size adapts to the LLM.Related chapter: 19

- Dual Reasoning: A GNN-LLM Collaborative Framework for Knowledge Graph Question Answering. Liu et al., 2024 arXiv 2406.01145Dual Reasoning (earlier titled "Explore then Determine"): a GNN explores the knowledge graph, then an LLM determines the answer from the pruned candidates.Related chapter: 19

- Knowledge-Augmented Language Model Prompting for Zero-Shot Knowledge Graph Question Answering. Baek et al., 2023 arXiv 2306.04136KAPING: retrieves KG facts relevant to the question and prepends them to the prompt for zero-shot KGQA, without training.Related chapters: 20, 22

- Text2Cypher: Bridging Natural Language and Graph Databases. Ozsoy et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.10064Neo4j's Text2Cypher dataset: combines existing text-to-Cypher resources into one cleaned benchmark and fine-tunes models on it.Chapter: 20

- Auto-Cypher: Improving LLMs on Cypher generation via LLM-supervised generation-verification framework. Tiwari et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.12612A generate-and-verify pipeline that synthesizes Text2Cypher training data with LLM supervision. Earlier titled "SynthCypher".Chapters: 20, 24, 33, C4

- CypherBench: Towards Precise Retrieval over Full-scale Modern Knowledge Graphs in the LLM Era. Feng et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.18702CypherBench: property-graph views of large knowledge graphs and a text-to-Cypher benchmark for precise retrieval.Related chapter: 20

- A Benchmark to Understand the Role of Knowledge Graphs on Large Language Model's Accuracy for Question Answering on Enterprise SQL Databases. Sequeda et al., 2023 arXiv 2311.07509A benchmark over an insurance SQL database: GPT-4 answers far more questions correctly when it queries a knowledge graph representation of the database than when it writes SQL directly.Chapters: 5, C4

- BYOKG-RAG: Multi-Strategy Graph Retrieval for Knowledge Graph Question Answering. Mavromatis et al., 2025 arXiv 2507.04127BYOKG-RAG: the LLM proposes entities, candidate answers, paths and OpenCypher queries; graph tools link them to a custom KG and retrieve context iteratively.Related chapter: 20

- HybridRAG: Integrating Knowledge Graphs and Vector Retrieval Augmented Generation for Efficient Information Extraction. Sarmah et al., 2024 arXiv 2408.04948HybridRAG: combines vector retrieval and knowledge graph retrieval for question answering over financial earnings call transcripts.Chapters: 21, 32, C4

- HybGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases. Lee et al., 2024 arXiv 2412.16311HybGRAG: a retriever bank and a critic let the system answer questions that need both textual and relational knowledge.Chapter: 33

- Knowledge Graph-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation. Zhu et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.06864KG2RAG: expands chunk retrieval along knowledge-graph links between chunks, then organizes the result into coherent paragraphs.Related chapter: 21

- Multi-Meta-RAG: Improving RAG for Multi-Hop Queries using Database Filtering with LLM-Extracted Metadata. Poliakov and Shvai, 2024 arXiv 2406.13213Multi-Meta-RAG: filters the retrieval database with LLM-extracted metadata (such as source and date) to improve multi-hop queries.Related chapter: 21

## Integration and reasoning

Getting graph evidence into the model's reasoning: graph chain-of-thought, faithful paths, constrained decoding and post-retrieval refinement.

- Graph Chain-of-Thought: Augmenting Large Language Models by Reasoning on Graphs. Jin et al., 2024 arXiv 2404.07103Graph Chain-of-Thought: the LLM iterates reasoning, choosing graph functions, and reading their results, and introduces the GRBench dataset.Chapters: 23, 33

- Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning. Luo et al., 2023 arXiv 2310.01061Reasoning on Graphs: plan relation paths, retrieve the valid paths from the KG, then reason over them faithfully.Chapters: 5, 18, 19, 23, 24, 33

- Graph-constrained Reasoning: Faithful Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs with Large Language Models. Luo et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.13080Graph-constrained Reasoning: a KG-Trie constrains decoding so the LLM can only generate reasoning paths that exist in the graph.Chapter: 23

- Decoding on Graphs: Faithful and Sound Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs through Generation of Well-Formed Chains. Li et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.18415Decoding on Graphs: graph-aware constrained decoding makes the LLM generate well-formed chains of connected triples.Chapter: 23

- Boosting Language Models Reasoning with Chain-of-Knowledge Prompting. Wang et al., 2023 arXiv 2306.06427Chain-of-Knowledge prompting: elicit evidence triples as reasoning steps and verify their factuality and faithfulness.Chapter: 23

- Chain-of-Knowledge: Grounding Large Language Models via Dynamic Knowledge Adapting over Heterogeneous Sources. Li et al., 2024 ICLR 2024Corrects rationales step by step with knowledge retrieved from heterogeneous sources, including structured queries such as SPARQL.Chapter: 23

- Mitigating Large Language Model Hallucinations via Autonomous Knowledge Graph-based Retrofitting. Guan et al., 2023 arXiv 2311.13314KGR: autonomously retrofits LLM drafts by extracting claims, checking them against a knowledge graph and revising.Related chapter: 23

- CoTKR: Chain-of-Thought Enhanced Knowledge Rewriting for Complex Knowledge Graph Question Answering. Wu et al., 2024 arXiv 2409.19753CoTKR: rewrites retrieved KG knowledge into chain-of-thought style text that better supports the question.Related chapters: 22, 23

- Empowering GraphRAG with Knowledge Filtering and Integration. Guo et al., 2025 arXiv 2503.13804GraphRAG-FI: filters noisy retrieved graph knowledge and integrates it with the LLM's own knowledge when retrieval is unhelpful.Related chapters: 22, 23

- HyperTree Planning: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Hierarchical Thinking. Gui et al., 2025 arXiv 2505.02322HyperTree Planning: hypertree-structured planning outlines for divide-and-conquer reasoning on complex planning tasks.Related chapter: 23

- KnowledGPT: Enhancing Large Language Models with Retrieval and Storage Access on Knowledge Bases. Wang et al., 2023 arXiv 2308.11761KnowledGPT: LLMs generate programs to search and store in knowledge bases, including a personalized knowledge base.Related chapters: 23, 30

## Training with graphs

Graph tokens, graph instruction tuning, and reinforcement learning for graph retrievers and constructors.

- GraphGPT: Graph Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models. Tang et al., 2023 arXiv 2310.13023GraphGPT: a graph-text alignment projector and two-stage graph instruction tuning.Chapters: 24, 33

- LLaGA: Large Language and Graph Assistant. Chen et al., 2024 arXiv 2402.08170LLaGA: node neighborhoods reorganized into structure-aware sequences and projected into the LLM's token space.Chapters: 24, 33

- Graph-oriented Instruction Tuning of Large Language Models for Generic Graph Mining. Tan et al., 2024 arXiv 2403.04780MuseGraph: compact graph descriptions and diverse instruction data (with chain-of-thought) for tuning LLMs on generic graph mining tasks.Chapters: 24, 33

- Graph Neural Prompting with Large Language Models. Tian et al., 2023 arXiv 2309.15427Graph Neural Prompting: a GNN encodes retrieved KG subgraphs into a soft prompt for a frozen LLM.Related chapter: 24

- Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning. Luo et al., 2025 arXiv 2507.21892Graph-R1: agentic GraphRAG over a lightweight hypergraph, trained with end-to-end reinforcement learning for multi-turn retrieval.Chapters: 24, 33

- LightPROF: A Lightweight Reasoning Framework for Large Language Model on Knowledge Graph. Ao et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.03137LightPROF: a small trainable adapter encodes retrieved reasoning graphs into soft prompts for a frozen LLM on KGQA.Related chapter: 24

- How to Make LMs Strong Node Classifiers?. Xu et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.02296Shows text-only LMs can become strong node classifiers by adding topological and semantic retrieval to their inputs, without graph-specific architectures.Related chapter: 24

- DRAG: Distilling RAG for SLMs from LLMs to Transfer Knowledge and Mitigate Hallucination via Evidence and Graph-based Distillation. Chen et al., 2025 arXiv 2506.01954DRAG: distills RAG ability from large to small models using ranked evidence and knowledge-graph-based distillation.Chapter: 24

## Evaluation and benchmarks

How to measure GraphRAG fairly, and where graphs actually help.

- When to use Graphs in RAG: A Comprehensive Analysis for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Xiang et al., 2025 arXiv 2506.05690GraphRAG-Bench: tasks of increasing difficulty (fact retrieval to creative generation) to test when graphs help RAG and when they do not.Chapters: 16, 25, 33, C1

- In-depth Analysis of Graph-based RAG in a Unified Framework. Zhou et al., 2025 arXiv 2503.04338DIGIMON: a unified framework that re-implements many graph-based RAG methods and compares them under the same settings.Chapters: 6, 16, 25, 28, 33

- RAG vs. GraphRAG: A Systematic Evaluation and Key Insights. Han et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.11371A systematic comparison of RAG and GraphRAG across QA and summarization tasks, with guidance on when each wins and how to combine them.Related chapter: 25

- LEGO-GraphRAG: Modularizing Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Design Space Exploration. Cao et al., 2024 arXiv 2411.05844LEGO-GraphRAG: splits GraphRAG retrieval into modules so the design space can be explored and compared systematically.Related chapters: 25, 33

- MultiHop-RAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Queries. Tang and Yang, 2024 arXiv 2401.15391MultiHop-RAG: a news-based benchmark of inference, comparison, temporal and null queries for multi-hop retrieval.Chapters: 3, 25, 33, C1

- CRUD-RAG: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models. Lyu et al., 2024 arXiv 2401.17043CRUD-RAG: a Chinese RAG benchmark organized by create, read, update and delete style tasks.Chapter: 25

- STaRK: Benchmarking LLM Retrieval on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases. Wu et al., 2024 arXiv 2404.13207STaRK: retrieval benchmark over semi-structured knowledge bases that mix text and relations (products, papers, biomedicine).Related chapters: 21, 25

- CRAG -- Comprehensive RAG Benchmark. Yang et al., 2024 arXiv 2406.04744CRAG: a factual QA benchmark with mock web and knowledge graph search APIs, spanning domains, question types and fact popularity.Related chapter: 25

- Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation. Es et al., 2023 arXiv 2309.15217Ragas: reference-free metrics for RAG pipelines such as faithfulness, answer relevance and context relevance.Chapter: 25

- ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems. Saad-Falcon et al., 2023 arXiv 2311.09476ARES: trains lightweight LLM judges on synthetic data and uses a small human-labeled set for confidence intervals.Chapter: 25

- MemoRAG: Boosting Long Context Processing with Global Memory-Enhanced Retrieval Augmentation. Qian et al., 2024 arXiv 2409.05591MemoRAG: a global memory model drafts clues to guide retrieval; the paper also introduces the UltraDomain evaluation set used by LightRAG-style comparisons.Related chapter: 25

## Cost and efficiency

Where indexing and query tokens go, and designs that spend fewer of them.

- LazyGraphRAG: Setting a new standard for quality and cost. Microsoft Research, 2024 blogDefers all LLM use to query time; indexing uses lightweight concept extraction, so its cost is close to vector RAG.Chapters: 6, 8, 12, 26, 28

- KET-RAG: A Cost-Efficient Multi-Granular Indexing Framework for Graph-RAG. Huang et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.09304KET-RAG: builds a full knowledge graph skeleton only for key chunks and a cheap text-keyword bipartite graph for the rest.Chapter: 33

- E²GraphRAG: Streamlining Graph-based RAG for High Efficiency and Effectiveness. Zhao et al., 2025 arXiv 2505.24226E²GraphRAG: a summary tree plus an entity graph built with fewer LLM calls, with adaptive local or global retrieval.Related chapter: 26

- LinearRAG: Linear Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation on Large-scale Corpora. Zhuang et al., 2025 arXiv 2510.10114LinearRAG: a relation-free graph of entities and passages that avoids costly relation extraction and scales linearly.Chapters: 6, 33

- Optimizing the Interface Between Knowledge Graphs and LLMs for Complex Reasoning. Markovic et al., 2025 arXiv 2505.24478Systematic hyperparameter tuning of a KG-plus-LLM pipeline (Cognee) on multi-hop QA benchmarks, showing that tuning gains are real but uneven.Related chapter: 28

## Temporal, incremental and memory

Graphs that change: bi-temporal facts, invalidation and long-term memory for agents.

- Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory. Rasmussen et al., 2025 arXiv 2501.13956Zep: Graphiti's temporal knowledge graph for agent memory, with episodes, bi-temporal edges and fact invalidation.Chapters: 27, 30, C3

- MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems. Packer et al., 2023 arXiv 2310.08560MemGPT: an operating-system view of LLM memory that pages information between the context window and external storage.Chapters: 27, 30, C3

- A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents. Xu et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.12110A-MEM: Zettelkasten-style linked memory notes that evolve as new memories arrive.Chapters: 30, C3

- Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory. Chhikara et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.19413Mem0: extracts, consolidates and retrieves conversation memories, including a graph-based variant.Related chapters: 30, C3

- T-GRAG: A Dynamic GraphRAG Framework for Resolving Temporal Conflicts and Redundancy in Knowledge Retrieval. Li et al., 2025 arXiv 2508.01680T-GRAG: a time-aware GraphRAG that models how knowledge evolves and resolves temporal conflicts and redundancy during retrieval.Related chapter: 27

## Agentic GraphRAG

LLM agents that build, search and reason over graphs with tools.

- GraphReader: Building Graph-based Agent to Enhance Long-Context Abilities of Large Language Models. Li et al., 2024 arXiv 2406.14550GraphReader: splits long text into a graph of key elements and atomic facts, then an agent explores it with planned actions and a notebook.Chapters: 30, 33

- GraphSearch: An Agentic Deep Searching Workflow for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Yang et al., 2025 arXiv 2509.22009GraphSearch: a six-module agentic deep-search workflow with dual-channel retrieval over chunk text and graph structure.Chapters: 30, 33

- Agentic Deep Graph Reasoning Yields Self-Organizing Knowledge Networks. Buehler, 2025 arXiv 2502.13025An agent iteratively expands its own knowledge graph; the graph self-organizes into a scale-free network with hubs and bridging nodes.Chapter: 30

- Agentic Reasoning: A Streamlined Framework for Enhancing LLM Reasoning with Agentic Tools. Wu et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.04644Agentic Reasoning: augments reasoning models with web search, code execution and a Mind-Map agent that keeps a knowledge graph of the reasoning context.Chapter: 30

- Affordable AI Assistants with Knowledge Graph of Thoughts. Besta et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.02670Knowledge Graph of Thoughts: an assistant that builds a task-specific knowledge graph with tools and reasons over it, cutting cost versus large models.Chapter: 30

- AGENTiGraph: An Interactive Knowledge Graph Platform for LLM-based Chatbots Utilizing Private Data. Zhao et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.11531AGENTiGraph: a multi-agent platform for managing and querying knowledge graphs through natural language, with real-time visualization.Chapter: 30

- G-Designer: Architecting Multi-agent Communication Topologies via Graph Neural Networks. Zhang et al., 2024 arXiv 2410.11782G-Designer: a GNN designs the communication topology of a multi-agent system for each task.Related chapter: 30

- A Practical Approach for Building Production-Grade Conversational Agents with Workflow Graphs. Park et al., 2025 arXiv 2505.23006Workflow graphs for production conversational agents that must follow service constraints, from an e-commerce case study.Related chapter: 30

- Graph RAG-Tool Fusion. Lumer et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.07223Graph RAG-Tool Fusion: retrieves tools with vector search, then follows a tool knowledge graph to pull in their dependencies.Related chapter: 30

## Multimodal and hypergraph

N-ary facts as hyperedges, and images, tables and video as graph nodes.

- HyperGraphRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Hypergraph-Structured Knowledge Representation. Luo et al., 2025 arXiv 2503.21322HyperGraphRAG: represents n-ary facts as hyperedges and retrieves entities and hyperedges together.Chapters: 6, 31, 33

- Hyper-RAG: Combating LLM Hallucinations using Hypergraph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Feng et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.08758Hyper-RAG: hypergraph-driven retrieval that captures pairwise and beyond-pairwise correlations, applied to medical knowledge.Related chapters: 31, 32

- RAG-Anything: All-in-One RAG Framework. Guo et al., 2025 arXiv 2510.12323RAG-Anything: one framework for text, images, tables and equations using dual graphs for cross-modal and textual relations.Related chapter: 31

- MMGraphRAG: Bridging Vision and Language with Interpretable Multimodal Knowledge Graphs. Wan and Yu, 2025 arXiv 2507.20804MMGraphRAG: builds a multimodal knowledge graph by linking scene graphs of images to a text knowledge graph.Related chapter: 31

- VideoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Extreme Long-Context Videos. Ren et al., 2025 arXiv 2502.01549VideoRAG: graph-based indexing of knowledge from extremely long videos combined with multimodal context encoding.Related chapter: 31

- RAG over Tables: Hierarchical Memory Index, Multi-Stage Retrieval, and Benchmarking. Zou et al., 2025 arXiv 2504.01346RAG over tables: a hierarchical memory index and multi-stage retrieval for heterogeneous documents with many tables.Related chapter: 31

## Domain applications

Code, medicine, customer service, finance and science.

## 2026 frontier papers

Recent preprints (2026) that point where the field is heading. Treat results as preliminary until replicated.

- MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG. Lee et al., 2026 arXiv 2609.11065MOSAIC: training-free; an LLM analyzer turns each query into a bounded exploration policy over seeds, traversal, stopping and evidence selection.Chapters: 30, 33

- LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Coll Tejeda et al., 2026 arXiv 2609.10239LiteRAG: replaces retrieval-time LLM control with query-conditioned algorithmic exploration and reasoning-chain context construction.Chapters: 26, 33

- NS-ST-GraphRAG: Neuro-Symbolic Spatio-Temporal GraphRAG for Literary Knowledge Processing. Lin, 2026 arXiv 2609.05139NS-ST-GraphRAG: ontology-guided extraction with dual temporal coordinates and spatial attributes; retrieves the graph state valid for a query's time and place.Chapter: 33

- Beyond Vector Search: Comparing Classical RAG with Hybrid GraphRAG for Climate Science Q&A. Naiff et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.28766A hybrid of vector search, GraphRAG with Leiden communities and cross-encoder reranking, compared with classical RAG on climate science questions.Chapter: 0

- From Extraction to Governed Memory: Multi-Agent Knowledge Graph Construction with Domain-Expert Review. Bykampadi et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.28642MAGG: multi-agent knowledge graph construction where domain owners review candidate triples and admitted facts carry audit metadata.Chapters: 29, 30

- post-graph-rag: A PostgreSQL-Native Bi-Temporal Graph RAG Engine with Temporal Grounding at Synthesis. Rajah, 2026 arXiv 2608.24921post-graph-rag: one PostgreSQL database with pgvector and edge tables, validated extraction, and a bi-temporal layer for superseded facts.Chapters: 27, 29, 33, C3

- Search Broadly, Seek Evidence on Both Sides, Decide Narrowly: Evidence-Admissible GraphRAG for Longitudinal Clinical Event Verification. Lin et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.22062MedEventGraph-RAG: an evidence-admissible design that gathers supporting and contradicting evidence for clinical event relations from patient-specific graphs.Chapters: 29, 32

- The Commercial Tax: Rent-vs-Own Blind Spots in Multi-Hop Retrieval Benchmarks. Sanchez and Dehnad, 2026 arXiv 2608.16096Audits multi-hop retrieval benchmarks for what buyers need: whether the embedders behind top results may be used commercially and what systems cost to build.Chapters: 25, 26, 29, 33

- LineageRAG: Harnessing GraphRAG by Constructing Evidence Lineages with Source Grounding. Zheng et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.16004LineageRAG: builds one evidence lineage per evidence demand and completes supported demands with verbatim source spans.Chapters: 29, 33

- Noesis: Bidirectional Graph-RAG with Adaptive Parallelism and Cross-Knowledge-Base Semantic Discovery. Cogotti, 2026 arXiv 2608.15919Noesis: bidirectional graph traversal for context resolution, adaptive ingestion concurrency, and routing across multiple knowledge bases.Related chapters: 26, 29

- Operationalizing Cyber Threat Intelligence with GraphRAG. Kabra et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.13050Compares Microsoft GraphRAG with naive RAG for turning cyber threat reports into detection plans that rely on durable behavioral clues.Chapter: 32

- HC-RAG: Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Heterogeneous Financial Filings. Chen et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.12335HC-RAG: a typed financial evidence graph over annual reports (documents, sections, text and table units) with document-section-unit retrieval paths.Chapters: 31, 32

- VDGR-RAG: Vectors, Directories, Graphs, and Reflection Are All You Need for Unified Reasoning over Hierarchical Enterprise Knowledge. Chen et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.07994VDGR-RAG: an agentic system that combines vectors, directory-structure reasoning, graph traversal and reflection for enterprise documentation.Related chapters: 21, 30

- DocNavRAG: Document-Structured Graph RAG with Stateful Evidence Construction for Complex Document Question Answering. Xie et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.01565DocNavRAG: an agent navigates a document-structure graph with locate, navigate, expand and fetch operations while tracking an evidence state.Chapter: 31

- HVM-GraphRAG: Holistic-View Multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Complex Document. He et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.24861HVM-GraphRAG: a compact concept-level graph indexed to multimodal chunks, avoiding traversal over dense entity graphs.Chapters: 31, 33

- HyCE-RAG: Hypergraph Chain-of-Evidence Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering. An et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.22597HyCE-RAG: builds a query-aware evidence hypergraph and propagates confidence over it for explainable multi-hop QA.Chapters: 31, 33

- Structure Over Scale: Schema-Constrained Causal Graphs for RAG. Saouda et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.22592HCG-RAG: schema-constrained causal graphs that are much smaller and cheaper to build than open-ended entity-relation graphs, and auditable by experts.Chapter: 26

- Optimizing Hypergraph-Based RAG: Toward Better Fact Extraction and Chunk Retrieval. Khrouf et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.20506Improves HyperGraphRAG with self-consistency prompting for fact extraction and Personalized PageRank over the hypergraph for chunk retrieval.Chapter: 31

- PAGE-RAG: Evidence-Grounded Adaptive Graph Retrieval for Long-Document Question Answering. Chen et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.19301PAGE-RAG: treats the graph as a skeleton over the source document, with task-adaptive routing and strict grounding boundaries.Related chapter: 22

- ColGraphRAG: Late-Interaction Evidence Retrieval for Multimodal GraphRAG. Kim, 2026 arXiv 2607.16208ColGraphRAG: late-interaction multi-vector scoring for image nodes in a multimodal evidence graph.Chapters: 31, 33

- EvoGraph-R1: Self-Evolving Multimodal Knowledge Hypergraphs for Agentic Retrieval. Lin et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.12764EvoGraph-R1: multimodal knowledge hypergraphs that an RL-trained agent updates and refines while it retrieves.Chapter: 31

- RAGU: A Multi-Step GraphRAG Engine with a Compact Domain-Adapted LLM. Komarov et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.11683RAGU: open-source engine with two-stage typed extraction, DBSCAN deduplication, Leiden communities and a compact 7B domain-adapted extractor.Chapter: 26

- NGM-RAG: Neural Graph Matching based Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Chen et al., 2026 arXiv 2607.11159NGM-RAG: neural graph matching that combines text matching with GNNs to retrieve graph evidence.Related chapter: 19

- Multi-Granularity Context-Enhanced RAG over Multimodal Knowledge Graphs. Wu et al., 2026 arXiv 2608.25986Uses textual context during visual extraction to build multimodal knowledge graphs with less semantic gap, for multi-granularity RAG.Chapter: 31

## Datasets

Question sets you can evaluate on. Match the dataset to the question type your users ask.

- HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering. Yang et al., 2018 arXiv 1809.09600HotpotQA: Wikipedia questions that need two supporting paragraphs, with sentence-level supporting facts.Chapters: 3, 17, 25, 33

- MuSiQue: Multihop Questions via Single-hop Question Composition. Trivedi et al., 2021 arXiv 2108.00573MuSiQue: 2 to 4 hop questions composed from single-hop questions, built to resist shortcut reasoning.Chapters: 17, 25, 30, 33

- Constructing A Multi-hop QA Dataset for Comprehensive Evaluation of Reasoning Steps. Ho et al., 2020 arXiv 2011.010602WikiMultiHopQA: multi-hop questions over Wikipedia and Wikidata with evidence paths.Chapters: 17, 25, 33

- MultiHop-RAG dataset. Tang and Yang, 2024 GitHubCode and data for the MultiHop-RAG news benchmark.Chapters: 3, 25, 33, C1

- GraphRAG-Bench. Xiang et al., 2025 GitHubData and evaluation code for the When-to-use-graphs benchmark.Chapters: 16, 25, 33

- PolyG and PolyBench. Liu et al., 2025 GitHubBenchmark and code covering four classes of graph questions.Chapter: 30

- CRUD-RAG. Lyu et al., 2024 GitHubData and code for the CRUD-RAG benchmark.Chapter: 25

- STaRK. Wu et al., 2024 GitHubSemi-structured retrieval benchmark data and code.Related chapter: 25

- Variational Reasoning for Question Answering with Knowledge Graph. Zhang et al., 2017 arXiv 1709.04071Introduces MetaQA, a movie knowledge graph QA dataset with 1, 2 and 3 hop questions, used to test KGQA methods.Chapter: 25

- FactKG: Fact Verification via Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs. Kim et al., 2023 arXiv 2305.06590FactKG: claims to verify by reasoning over DBpedia, with one-hop, conjunction, existence, multi-hop and negation types.Chapter: 25

- The Value of Semantic Parse Labeling for Knowledge Base Question Answering (WebQSP). Yih et al., 2016 ACLWebQuestionsSP: Freebase questions annotated with SPARQL-style semantic parses, a standard KGQA benchmark.Chapters: 18, 19, 20, 25

- The Web as a Knowledge-Base for Answering Complex Questions (ComplexWebQuestions). Talmor and Berant, 2018 NAACLComplexWebQuestions: compositional questions built from WebQSP, a standard multi-hop KGQA benchmark.Chapters: 18, 19, 25

- neo4j/text2cypher-2024v1. Neo4j, 2024 Hugging FaceThe Text2Cypher training and test set released with Neo4j's Text2Cypher paper.Chapter: 20

- Loong. Wang et al., 2024 GitHubLong-context multi-document QA benchmark in which every document matters to the answer.Related chapter: 25
